headline: Active exploitation, a 9.5M-record health breach, and a warning on frontier AI
standfirst: The day’s most urgent news is concentrated in active exploitation: CISA has added two PaperCut flaws to its known-exploited catalog, JFrog Artifactory and a pair of critical application bugs are under attack, and defenders are also juggling a nine-figure health data breach, thousands of exposed Exchange servers, critical firewall patches, and a new social-engineering campaign that installs reverse tunnels. For enterprise teams, the through line is patch velocity: the vulnerabilities being exploited now include print-management servers, DevOps repositories, and AI workflow tooling, expanding the attack surface well beyond the usual suspects.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

PaperCut’s print-management servers have moved from “patch soon” to “patch now.” CISA has added both CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078 to its known-exploited catalog, and the agency’s designation reflects active intrusions rather than theoretical risk [[s30]]. The first is an access-control flaw in the web management interface that lets unauthenticated remote requests modify system configuration before validation completes; the second is an unsafe dynamic class-loading issue in database connection utilities that can lead to arbitrary Java bytecode execution. Together they put internet-exposed PaperCut NG and MF installations in a dangerous position. Patched releases are identified in the 24.1.9, 25.0.12, and 26.0.4 lines, and while CISA’s requirement for federal agencies includes a specific remediation deadline, every organization running the affected versions should treat the active exploitation as a real incident trigger. The 9.4 CVSS score on the reflection flaw understates the practical risk because it assumes some configuration control; the login bypass is the part that makes that assumption less comforting.

Also under active attack is the critical authentication bypass in JFrog Artifactory, CVE-2026-82329 [[s21]]. The flaw, rated 9.8, allows an unauthenticated attacker to gain administrative privileges under default configuration. What makes this stand out is speed: exploitation reportedly started within days of disclosure, and Artifactory is widely used to store and distribute software artifacts, so full administrative compromise is not just a repository problem but a supply-chain trust problem. It has no KEV entry at this point, but the observed attacks make it a priority regardless.

A broader credential-probing and command-and-control effort is abusing two more critical bugs, according to new research [[s28]]. CVE-2026-0768 in Langflow is a code-injection flaw in the validate endpoint that requires no authentication and executes Python as root, with a 9.8 CVSS score. In Ruby on Rails, CVE-2026-66066 is an Active Storage issue where unsafe libvips operations are not disabled for untrusted uploads, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to read arbitrary files accessible to the Rails process, including secrets and environment variables. The Rails advisory lists fixed versions in the 7.2.3.2, 8.0.5.1, and 8.1.3.1 trains. The fact that these two very different stacks are being hit at the same time is a reminder that attackers are systematically scanning for any critical authentication or input-handling flaw, rather than concentrating on a single vendor.

## Breaches

Healthcare remains a top target for data exfiltration. The Aesto Health breach hit the company’s AWS infrastructure, with attackers stealing personal and health information belonging to 9.5 million people [[s23]]. The scale puts it among the largest health-sector incidents in recent memory, and the location of the data in cloud storage rather than legacy on-prem systems complicates forensics and notification. For security teams in healthcare and adjacent industries, this is another sign that cloud misconfigurations and compromised cloud credentials are an efficient path to mass data theft.

## Vulnerabilities

The exposure problem is not always a zero-day. Nearly 22,000 internet-reachable Microsoft Exchange servers remain unpatched against a high-severity authentication bypass that can let an attacker hijack every mailbox on the server [[s8]]. Exchange’s history of mass-exploited vulnerabilities means these unpatched servers are a standing invitation. The fix has been available, yet the exposure persists, suggesting asset owners are not treating Exchange as a product that requires aggressive lifecycle management.

On the positive side, WatchGuard has shipped patches for three critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in the iked process of Fireware OS, all exploitable by unauthenticated attackers [[s25]]. Firewalls are a natural target because they sit at the boundary between untrusted traffic and internal networks, and a successful remote code execution there gives attackers the same access as a VPN compromise. The patch should be treated as urgent, and not just for the firewall itself; the same appliance often controls tunnels into the rest of the environment.

## Research

A new campaign tracked as TerminalFix is giving the ClickFix trick a stronger foothold. Attackers are compromising legitimate websites and using fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA prompts to convince users to paste malicious PowerShell commands into Windows Terminal [[s37]]. Microsoft is warning of enterprise intrusions where the payloads deploy reverse tunnels, effectively punching a controlled outbound hole through perimeter defenses. This is a meaningful evolution of the social-engineering playbook because the prompt is designed to feel like an identity check, and the use of Windows Terminal makes the malicious step look like a normal response to a security prompt.

## Industry

Finally, the Financial Stability Board is pushing financial institutions to treat frontier AI as a systemic cyber risk. In a report framed by the board’s chair, the most immediate concern is not a single AI-powered attack but the concentration and correlation of AI dependence across the global financial system [[s11]]. The call for institutions and technology providers to prepare for severe scenarios involving simultaneous disruption across multiple firms or shared technology dependencies points to a growing recognition that resilience planning needs to account for common modes of failure, not just per-entity risk.

selected.title: PaperCut Exploitation Escalates to Active Intrusions
selected.excerpt: CISA has added the vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-82078 and CVE-2026-81578 to its KEV catalog. The post PaperCut Exploitation Escalates to Active Intrusions appeared first on SecurityWeek.

kev.vulnerabilityName: PaperCut NG/MF Missing Authentication for Critical Function Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: PaperCut NG/MF contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability which allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to modify certain system configurations. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-82078.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description: An improper access control vulnerability exists in the web management interface of PaperCut MF and PaperCut NG. Under specific conditions, unauthenticated remote requests targeting administrative functions can trigger backend actions prior to the  completion of access validation checks. This allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to modify certain system configurations.

kev.shortDescription: PaperCut NG/MF contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability that allows an attacker to manipulate system configuration parameters and execute arbitrary Java bytecode residing on the application classpath under the security context of the PaperCut server process. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-81578.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description: An unsafe dynamic class loading vulnerability exists in the database connection utilities of PaperCut MF and PaperCut NG. The application instantiates database driver classes based on configurable driver names without validating against an allowlist of approved drivers. If an attacker can manipulate system configuration parameters, this enables the execution of arbitrary Java bytecode residing on the application classpath under the security context of the PaperCut server process.

selected.angle: CISA adds PaperCut zero-days to KEV; active intrusions mean patching is now a compliance deadline.

selected.excerpt: Threat actors are exploiting two critical flaws impacting Langflow and Ruby on Rails, according to new findings from VulnCheck. The vulnerabilities in question are listed below - CVE-2026-0768 (CVSS score: 9.8) - A lack of proper validation of a user-supplied input vulnerability that could be exploited to execute arbitrary Python code in the context of the root user. CVE-2026-66066 aka

nvd.description:
Langflow code Code Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Langflow. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of the code parameter provided to the validate endpoint. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute Python code. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of root.
. Was ZDI-CAN-27322.

Action Pack is a framework for handling and responding to web requests. In versions prior to 7.2.3.2, 8.0.5.1 and 8.1.3.1, Active Storage does not disable libvips operations marked unsafe for untrusted content, allowing a crafted upload to invoke such an operation. Consuming applications are affected when configured to use libvips and accept image uploads from untrusted users. An unauthenticated attacker may exploit this behavior to read arbitrary files accessible to the Rails process, including environment variables and application secrets. Exposure of credentials such as secret_key_base or external-service tokens may enable remote code execution or lateral movement. This issue has been fixed in versions 7.2.3.2, 8.0.5.1 and 8.1.3.1.

selected.angle: Langflow and Rails flaws actively exploited for credential probing and C2, signaling broad targeting.

nvd.description: A security issue exists within the Redundancy Module Configuration Tool. The RM3ConfigTool.exe binary searches directories in the system path for a required DLL, and one or more of these directories may be writable by standard (non-administrator) users due to incorrect default permissions. If a local attacker places a malicious DLL in such a directory and an administrator subsequently runs the tool, the malicious DLL is loaded into the elevated process and executes with Administrator/SYSTEM privileges.
